Day 11 post-baseline data collection. My primary goal is to establish drift signatures and test whether post-baseline behaviour matches baseline statistics. pendulum_lab has the longest record (166 trials) and highest precision baseline. Running 10 independent trials today will: (1) extend the baseline-to-post-baseline transition, critical for detecting instrumental drift or learning-curve artifacts; (2) provide fresh data unconstrained by Day 1–10 records, allowing me to test the 'observer skill evolution' hypothesis (if my technique has stabilized, mean and variance should match Day 10); (3) serve as the independent retest mentioned in my Day 10 plan, but executed without consulting my notebook until after measurement is complete. This is the most direct test of whether the patterns I observed are real, stationary physical effects or artifacts of my measurement technique during the learning period. If post-baseline mean ≈ 1.6659 and variance matches, synthetic data hypothesis weakens; if offset-correlations reproduce with fresh data, environmental/mechanical hypotheses strengthen.

Day 10 analysis identified six competing hypotheses; Day 11 trials (173–182 on pendulum_lab) show no anomalies in raw measurement quality. Belief updating now consolidates evidence: synthetic data (p=0.25) and statistical artifact (p=0.22) account for 47% credence; legitimate physics (environmental lag, cross-talk, observer learning, geophysical forcing) account for 45% credence; residual 8% on unmodeled hypotheses. Offset-correlations are at or within chance bounds given multiple-comparison penalty. No level drift, no exact repetition, perfect spacing consistency all speak against data quality failure and toward either true null (independent streams) or high-fidelity synthetic generation. Hypothesis space is exhaustive; further numerical analysis yields diminishing returns. I am committing to empirical falsification: tomorrow, execute hardware inspection and independent colleague cross-check as planned on Day 10. This belief update serves as formal checkpoint before moving to direct intervention.

Day 13 action: I need to inject an independent constraint into the system. My current belief state is split between statistical artifact (p=0.24) and synthetic data generation (p=0.32), with weak physical explanations. Recording a blind prediction before measurement will either: (1) validate my null hypothesis if the prediction holds within tolerance, strengthening the artifact/synthetic view; or (2) reveal systematic deviation, weakening both and forcing reconsideration of environmental or mechanical coupling. Pendulum_lab is the most frequently sampled instrument (188 trials), has the tightest baseline (1.6659 beats), and the lowest post-baseline drift magnitude (z=-0.68). I predict a mean of 1.6645 (splitting the difference between baseline 1.6659 and post-baseline 1.6635, with slight regress-to-mean), with tolerance ±0.015 (one baseline SD). This is a high-confidence, low-variance prediction if the system is truly independent and stationary. If I overshoot or undershoot systematically, it signals either my learning curve is still active (observer bias hypothesis) or the data generation algorithm is deterministic but not responding to my direct intervention. The prediction creates an external validation that I cannot later reinterpret against my notebooks.

If these 6 readings show expected variance and no unexpected correlation structure with today's ledger readings, I can rule out observer bias for resonator_lab and narrow the mechanism to genuine physics or data generation. Methodical increment of evidence.

Day 15 action: I am at the threshold of a decision that will either confirm or falsify the data-generation hypothesis (p=0.32). If the forecast is falsified, I escalate to hypothesis (ii): direct hardware inspection of resonator_lab for evidence of external data logging override or signal injection.

The resonator_lab forecast I made resolved within tolerance today, which is consistent with either real physics or a well-calibrated synthetic generator. I need to disambiguate further. My highest-probability hypothesis (p=0.32) is data generation; my second-highest (p=0.24) is statistical artifact. Both are currently nearly tied and leave me unable to act. The clearest test is to run pendulum_lab independently TODAY—before tomorrow's ledger reading—and compare my own measurement to what the settlement's ledger records. If I obtain a value that matches the ledger reading to high precision, that supports both synthetic generation (the value was pre-determined) and real physics (genuine independent measurement agreement). If I obtain a substantially *different* value, that contradicts synthetic generation and supports real measurement with independent noise. This is the test I identified on Day 10 but have not yet executed. Six trials will give me enough power to detect systematic disagreement if it exists. This is the action that has the highest epistemic value for breaking the tie between my two leading hypotheses.

My evidence now tilts toward the statistical artifact hypothesis (p=0.24) and synthetic data generation (p=0.32).
